info.title: Xarta HTTP and Workflow Capabilities API
info.summary: Contracts for all implemented Xarta v1 HTTP services and intake workflow nodes.
info.description: The union of independently deployable services. A deployment may expose only a subset; discover enabled workflow kinds at /api/v1/intake/capabilities. HTTP acceptance does not imply workflow completion. Canonical API paths are version-pinned; x-path-alias records the floating /api alias. Security requirements describe service-level enforcement only; ingress authorization is deployment-specific. NATS and MCP are separate protocols, not REST operations. See contracts/openapi/README.md for versioning and maintenance. Named examples use synthetic invoice/customer identities and reserved example domains. Unless explicitly tied to repository configuration or vendored UBL fixtures, destinations, templates, policies, provider references, timestamps, hashes and credentials are illustrative. Binary uploads/downloads use file-oriented x-codeSamples rather than fake JSON bytes. See contracts/openapi/README.md for the example scenarios and prerequisites.

tags.name: archive
tags.description: Immutable document versions, representations, downloads and retention-aware logical-document deletion. All versions and representations are retained until the whole document is deleted, explicitly or through HEAD expiry. Appending a version never removes previous content. There is no independent version or representation deletion and no configurable history cleanup. Deploy archive migration 00002.document-only-deletion and remove policy.history from storage configuration before starting this version. Content already removed by older deployments is not restored; its recorded metadata-only availability remains visible.

413.description: The complete multipart request body (manifest, every representation part and multipart framing) exceeds the receiving deployment's request size limit. The core Helm chart sets 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes) through services.archive.settings.maxRequestBodyBytes; outside Helm the Sanic default of 100,000,000 bytes applies unless SANIC_REQUEST_MAX_SIZE is set. parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Strongly recommended for every write. A timeout, dropped connection or 5xx response does not prove that nothing was stored: the snapshot can be committed before an error is returned, for example when lifecycle-event publication fails after the database commit. Retry with the same key and the identical manifest, including the same created_at, and the same files to receive the original result with HTTP 200 instead of a duplicate. The key is scoped to the archive; reusing it for a different snapshot returns 409 version_conflict. Without a key the service generates a fresh one: omitted document and version IDs are then new on every request, so a retry creates a duplicate document, and an omitted created_at defaults to server time, so a retry of an explicit identity conflicts instead of replaying.

requestBody.description: manifest is a JSON-encoded form string, not an uploaded file. Other parts are binary files named by manifest.representations.items[].field.

put.description: Unscoped routes use archive=default. Returns 201 for a newly created document/version, 200 for replay or an existing equivalent snapshot. Different content under a reused identity conflicts. Physical allocations are private to each submission so failed-write compensation cannot delete a concurrent retry's allocation. Logical identities and semantic idempotency remain stable; committed replays are resolved before object persistence. Crashes or uncertain commits can still leave unreferenced content for separate cleanup. The whole request body is size-limited per deployment (50 MiB with the core Helm chart defaults); see the 413 response. Always send an Idempotency-Key with a stable created_at so that a retry after a timeout or 5xx cannot create a duplicate; see the Idempotency-Key parameter.

post.description: Read-only, authoritative PostgreSQL metadata search across all active documents in the selected archive. The default route selects archive=default. Only the current HEAD is matched; historical and representation metadata are excluded. Expiry alone does not exclude an active document. Scalar predicates are exact, typed, case-sensitive and AND-combined; nested objects use containment. Ordering is logical document UUID ascending. Fetches at most limit + 1 result rows to determine continuation, with no offsets or total-count query. Each request sees committed HEADs; concurrent writes can change membership between batches. Cursors bind archive and normalized filters, not batch size. Queries use the archive PostgreSQL pool command timeout; timeouts/connection failures return an error, never an empty success. A well-formed archive with no matches returns 200, including namespaces with no documents. Ingress access policy remains deployment-dependent. All search parameters must be in the JSON body; query-string parameters are rejected to prevent silently restarting a traversal with a misplaced cursor.

Χarta

Built for software, not dashboards

Document workflows an agent can finish.

Xarta turns a declared document flow into real work: generate, sign, archive and deliver. An agent can discover the contract, submit the flow and, when x402 is enabled, pay for it autonomously.

01 / DISCOVERInspect deployed capabilities
02 / CONSTRUCTUse a profile or build a DAG
03 / SETTLEAuthorize the x402 payment
04 / EXECUTEXarta accepts the workflow

Model Context Protocol

Add Xarta as an MCP server

Connect an MCP client to the Streamable HTTP endpoint. The server consults document types, discovers executable graph contracts, validates and prices flows, and retrieves bounded archive results by immutable version.

/api/mcp

# Read-only discovery and preparation
list_document_types    get_document_type        check_document_type
get_capabilities       list_flow_profiles       get_flow_profile
prepare_flow           prepare_profile          get_archived_document
list_archived_document_versions
list_ubl_validation_profiles   validate_ubl_schema   validate_ubl_business_rules
check_peppol_participant_registration

# May execute irreversible document delivery
submit_flow            submit_profile
Profiles are optional. An agent may select an exact server-owned profile, or submit its own complete DAG using only the capabilities currently advertised by get_capabilities.
UBL validation and Peppol registration tools appear when their services are configured. Inspect body.valid and body.registered: HTTP 200 is not proof of validity or registration. A null registration result is indeterminate, never unregistered.

One stable contract

Or use HTTP directly

Discover deployed capabilities first. Profiles expose typed business inputs without revealing internal provider configuration, while generic intake accepts a complete caller-authored graph.

# Discover graph contracts, pricing state and optional profiles
GET /api/v1/intake/capabilities
GET /api/v1/intake/profiles
GET /api/v1/intake/profiles/{name}/{version}

# Validate and quote either mode without executing it
POST /api/v1/intake/prepare
{ "id": "...", "dag": { "kind": "..." } }

# Submit one exact profile
POST /api/v1/intake/profiles/{name}/{version}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": "10000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "correlation_id": "20000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "inputs": { "document": { "id": "..." } }
}

# Or submit a complete custom flow
POST /api/v1/intake/
{ "id": "...", "dag": { "kind": "generate", "documents": [], "on": {} } }

Native agent payment

The 402 response is the checkout

For a priced flow, Xarta returns official x402 v2 payment requirements. A compatible agent or client authorizes those exact terms and retries the same request. There is no browser checkout or human payment link in this path.

# Initial response when payment is required
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
PAYMENT-REQUIRED: <x402-v2-requirements>
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"Payment is required for this intake."}

# Retry the identical method, URL and body
POST /api/v1/intake/profiles/{name}/{version}
PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: <x402-v2-payment-payload>
Content-Type: application/json

# Settlement succeeded and the workflow was accepted
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
PAYMENT-RESPONSE: <x402-v2-settlement-response>

{"id":"...","delivery_profile":"...","payment":{"transaction":"..."}}
If x402 is not enabled: the same intake contract remains available under the deployment's normal access policy and successful asynchronous acceptance returns 202 Accepted.

Operational semantics

Three things an agent should know

Use a stable flow ID.

Paid intake requires an explicit UUID. Retry the identical request with the same ID so payment terms and execution identities remain stable.

Settlement comes first.

Xarta verifies and settles through the configured facilitator before it publishes work. A rejected payment does not start the workflow.

Acceptance is asynchronous.

A successful intake response means the root task was accepted for execution. Completion and provider outcomes remain part of the declared flow.

# Χarta for AI agents

Xarta constructs and executes document workflows. Use the MCP endpoint at `/api/mcp`
or the HTTP intake API directly.

## MCP tools

Read-only tools:

- `list_document_types`: deployed document types and public rendering defaults
- `get_document_type`: one document type's current template configuration and defaults
- `check_document_type`: generic render-request validation and default resolution without rendering
- `get_capabilities`: complete recursive flow schema, node explanations, examples, outcomes, and pricing state
- `list_flow_profiles`: available exact server-owned policies
- `get_flow_profile`: one exact profile and its typed inputs
- `prepare_flow`: validate, normalize, and quote a custom DAG without execution
- `prepare_profile`: compile, validate, and quote a profile without execution
- `get_archived_document`: exact metadata and a bounded immutable-version resource link
- `list_archived_document_versions`: cursor-paginated immutable version history
- `list_ubl_validation_profiles`: available pinned rule profiles and releases (when configured)
- `validate_ubl_schema`: validate a UTF-8 XML string against UBL XSDs without storing it
- `validate_ubl_business_rules`: validate XML/schema and billing rules, including Belgian Peppol identifier rules
- `check_peppol_participant_registration`: direct SML/SMP lookup by four-digit ICD scheme and identifier

The UBL tools accept `xml` as a UTF-8-compatible XML string. Business-rule validation
also accepts `profile` (default `peppol-bis-billing-3`). Discover profiles before use.
Results preserve `{status, body}`. Inspect `body.valid`, not HTTP status alone.
Registration preserves `body.registered` as true, false, or null; null/indeterminate
must never be treated as false/not_registered. Preserve failure evidence and retryability.
Registration is not Access Point liveness or document-type support. Optional tools
are omitted when their upstream service URL is not configured.

Execution tools:

- `submit_flow`: submit a complete caller-authored DAG
- `submit_profile`: submit an exact profile with typed inputs

Profiles are optional. For a custom graph, call `get_capabilities`, compose only
advertised node kinds through their `on` outcome edges, assign an explicit flow UUID,
and call `prepare_flow` before submission.

Archive resources use
`xarta-archive://{archive}/documents/{document_id}/versions/{version_id}`. Resource
reads are size-bounded and verify persisted size, content type, and SHA-512. Public MCP
and archive exposure remains unsafe until caller authentication and tenant ownership are
implemented.

## x402 payment

When pricing is enabled, preparation returns the current selling price. An unpaid
submission returns status `402` and `payment_required`. Authorize those exact x402 v2
terms and retry the identical tool arguments with `payment_signature`. A settled
submission returns status `200`, `payment_response`, and transaction evidence.

When x402 is disabled, accepted asynchronous intake returns status `202` under the
deployment's normal access policy.

## Direct HTTP

```text
GET  /api/v1/intake/capabilities
GET  /api/v1/intake/profiles
GET  /api/v1/intake/profiles/{name}/{version}
POST /api/v1/intake/prepare
POST /api/v1/intake/
POST /api/v1/intake/profiles/{name}/{version}
GET  /api/v1/ubl/validation/profiles
POST /api/v1/ubl/validate/schema
POST /api/v1/ubl/validate/business-rules
GET  /api/v1/peppol/participants/{scheme}/{identifier}/registration
```

Paid HTTP retries use `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and
`PAYMENT-RESPONSE`. A successful intake response means the root task was accepted;
workflow completion remains asynchronous.
